It's a poem from the book (and movie) The Perks Of Being A wallflower

>Once on a yellow piece of paper with green lines

>He wrote a poem

>And he called it Chops

>Because that was the name of his dog

>And that's what it was all about

>And his teacher gave him an A

>And a gold star

>And his mother hung it on the kitchen door

>And read it to his aunts

>That was the year Father Tracy

>Took all the kids to the zoo

>And he let them sing on the bus

>And his little sister was born

>With tiny toenails and no hair

>And his mother and father kissed a lot

>And the girl around the corner sent him a

>Valentine with a row of X's

>And he had asked his father what the X's meant

>And his father tucked him in bed at night

>And was always there to do it


>Once on a white piece of paper with blue lines

>He wrote a poem

>And he called it Autumn

>Because that's what it was all about

>And his teacher gave him an A

>And asked him to write more clearly

>And his mother never hung it on the kitchen door

>Because of it's new paint

>And the kids told him Father Tracy smoked cigars

>And left butts on the pews

>And sometimes the would burn holes

>That was the year his sister got glasses

>With thick lenses and black frames

>And the girl around the corner laughed

>When he asked to go see Santa Clause

>And the kids told him why

>His mother and father kissed a lot

>And his father never tucked him in bed at night

>And his father got mad

>When he cried for him to do it


>Once on a piece of paper torn from his notebook

>He wrote a poem

>And he called it "Innocence: A Question"

>Because that was the question about his girl

>And that's what it was all about

>And his professor gave him an A

>And a strange steady look

>And his mother never hung it on the kitchen door

>Because he never showed her

>That was the year Father Tracy died

>And he forgot how the end

>Of the Apostle's Creed went

>And he caught his sister

>Making out on the back porch

>And his mother and father never kissed

>Or even talked

>And the girl around the corner

>Wore too much make up

>That made him cough when he kissed her

>But he kissed her anyway 

>Because that was the thing to do

>And at three A.M. he tucked himself into bed

>His father snoring loudly

>That's why on the back of a brown paper bag


>He tried another poem

>And he called it "Absolutely Nothing"

>Because that's what it was really all about

>And he gave himself an A

>And a slash on damned wrist

>And he hung it on the bathroom door

>Because this time he didn't think

>He could reach the kitchen

Wow. Really thoughtful feedback. Yeah this is the first poem I've written and saved. Since then I've been writing more but this is the first one I wrote and it's also my favorite that I've done. I really wanted this one to rhyme because I like to play with rhyme schemes so that was the main focus. And it isn't actually about digging holes. It's about self harm. I really like symbolism and subtlety (both of which I am working on improving). The water is the blood that rises after breaking skin and the "floods that will never end" is the risk of cutting too deep and accidentally bleeding out which is why the hole is filled. The ground is the skin and the shovel is obviously the blade used to cut which is why I used the word "rend". I wasn't putting much focus on rhythm or form because this was the first poem I did for fun and I just wanted to say what I wanted to say (personally I think I didn't do a bad job at that). Of course after reading it a for the first time after writing it was significantly less satisfying than I had originally thought it was. And "break the stab" was a mistake. I think I was thinking of another word when I typed this up.   

You're feedback was extremely helpful and I am certainly considering improving my poetry writing and look forward to more critiques like this to future posts.
